S68.01.needs: an account that has a cloud session, and the Desktop app
S68.01.note: Desktop app shows the same hosted web pages, so cloud sessions match by URL; local sessions are a separate list.
steps: Sign in, then click Code in the sidebar.
Click a session under Cloud sessions.
Note the session title and the address, which ends in /code/ and an ID.
Open the Desktop app, go to Code, and open the same session.
Compare the title and ID with the Expected line.
S68.01.where: Sidebar > Code > Cloud sessions > open a session

S68.02.needs: an account with a cloud session that has several messages, and the Desktop app
steps: Sign in, click Code in the sidebar, and click a session under Cloud sessions.
Scroll the conversation and note the last message.
Open the same session in the Desktop app's Code view.
Compare the conversation history and the last message with the Expected line.
S68.02.where: Sidebar > Code > Cloud sessions > open a session

S68.03.needs: a session linked to a git repository, and a second client
S68.03.note: The branch name is data from the session, so the exact name cannot be taken from the code.
steps: Click Code in the sidebar and open a session that has a repository.
Click the Changes button in the session header.
Read the branch shown next to the git branch icon (base, arrow, working branch).
Open the same session in the other client and check the same branch name appears.
Compare the branch with the Expected line.
S68.03.where: Sidebar > Code > open a session > Changes

S68.04.needs: a cloud session with a repository, and a second client
steps: Click Code in the sidebar and open a cloud session.
Read the small chip in the session header: network setting, then a dot and the repository name.
Open the same session in the other client and read the chip.
Compare the repository name on both clients with the Expected line.
S68.04.where: Sidebar > Code > open a session > header chip

S68.06.needs: an account that can see the Model for this agent dropdown, and a second client
S68.06.note: No code found for sharing instruction files across clients. The E2B gate cited in the plan is about sandbox provisioning, not model or instruction settings.
steps: Click Code in the sidebar, then New, and look at the composer.
Check the Model for this agent dropdown, shown only when models are offered.
Open the same session in the other client and compare the model shown.
S68.06.where: Code composer > Model for this agent

labels.text: Continue in VS Code or the terminal
To continue in the terminal, run this in the same folder:

S68.13.needs: the Desktop app with a local session; VS Code is optional for the link
S68.13.note: Only local sessions show this menu item; cloud sessions show Continue in VS Code in the Changes panel.
steps: Open the Desktop app, click Code, and open a local session.
Click the Session actions button (...) in the header.
Click Continue in VS Code or the terminal.
Look for the Continue in VS Code link and the text To continue in the terminal, run this in the same folder:, with a command below it.
Compare with the Expected line: the hand-off is explicit.
S68.13.where: Sidebar > Code > open a local session > Session actions (the ... button) > Continue in VS Code or the terminal

S68.14.needs: a phone with the mobile app and the Desktop app
S68.14.note: Desktop side is in Settings > Capabilities > Remote Control (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/RemoteControlSection.tsx), but I found no phone-side screen for continuing local execution in apps/desktop; the dispatcher line cited is a generic remote control start.

S68.15.needs: a paid account, and cloud execution enabled on the server
S68.15.note: Cloud execution depends on the E2B provisioning gate (apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts, e2bProvisioningReady). I could not find a desktop control that continues a cloud session from the local app beyond the shared Code page.

S68.17.needs: a cloud session that produced results, and a local folder
S68.17.note: Searched apps/web/features/code and apps/desktop/electron for return-to-local wording. apps/desktop/electron/windowPolicy.ts:85 only opens external links. The closest control is Apply to local (apps/web/features/code/local-code.ts:1610), which applies a local worktree, not cloud results.

S68.19.needs: a web browser and a Desktop app linked to the same account
steps: Sign in on a web browser (not the Desktop app, which hides this item).
Click Your computer in the Code sidebar.
Look for the heading Computers on your account and a list of computers.

S68.20.needs: a Desktop app linked to the account
S68.20.note: Rows are text lines; I did not confirm a card layout in the code.
steps: Click Settings, then Account.
Scroll to Linked devices.
Find a row for a Desktop app device and read its name, the surface label and its status.

S68.21.note: Code sessions are not in the capability list shown; the dispatcher line cited has moved.
steps: Click Settings, then Account, and scroll to Linked devices.
Find a device row and read its Can use line.
Compare the listed items (Browser, Computer use, Local models, Local MCP, Remote Control) with the Expected line.

S68.22.needs: a paid plan, and a phone or second browser
S68.22.note: The claim route needs signaling settings (apps/web/app/api/pair/claim/route.ts); the plan says it was not live-checked, and I did not confirm it.
steps: Click Settings, then Capabilities, and scroll to Remote Control.
Click Pair a phone.
Look for the pairing QR code and the Pairing code.
Pair the phone or a second browser, then check Settings > Account > Linked devices shows it.
Compare with the Expected line.
S68.22.where: Settings > Capabilities > Remote Control > Pair a phone

S68.23.needs: a paired phone, and a paid plan
steps: With a paired phone shown, click Settings, Capabilities, Remote Control.
Click Disconnect phone and read the confirmation dialog.
Click Disconnect phone in the dialog.
Check the phone stops working, and see Settings > Account > Linked devices, where the device row has an Unlink device button.
S68.23.where: Settings > Capabilities > Remote Control > Disconnect phone

S68.24.needs: a second client signed in to the account and a folder approved on the computer
S68.24.note: Approved folders are under Settings > Capabilities > Local access > Folders > Add a folder (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/LocalAccessSection.tsx), but I found no screen on another client that starts a session; the plan says that screen is unverified and Remote Control is hidden in mobile v1.

S68.25.needs: a linked computer that is offline or asleep
S68.25.note: Settings > Account > Linked devices shows only the word Offline; the explanation appears on the Your computer page.
steps: In a web browser, click Your computer in the Code sidebar.
Open a computer that is offline or asleep, and read its status after its name.
Read the message: Your computer went offline. This page reconnects when it is back.
Compare with the Expected line.

labels.text: Connection lost. Reconnecting so your phone can pick up where it left off.

S68.26.needs: a paired phone and a paid plan
S68.26.note: The reconnect message only shows while the status is reconnecting.
steps: With a phone paired, click Settings, Capabilities, Remote Control.
Turn off the phone's network for a moment.
Look for the message Connection lost. Reconnecting so your phone can pick up where it left off.
Turn the network back on and look for Connected to followed by the phone name.

S68.30.needs: two clients on the same account, and a session that needs approval
S68.30.note: The line says This browser only, which conflicts with the cross-client Expected; apps/desktop/electron/runtime/codeSessionActivity.ts is gone, so only the reporting in apps/desktop/electron/main.ts remains.
steps: Click Settings, then Notifications.
Find Agent run updates and read its line: Completions, failures and approval requests. This browser only.
Start an approval or a failing run in a session on another client.
Check whether this client shows a notification.
